title: Planar convexity and disk rigidity for finite-moment nonlocal perimeter minimizers by critical-energy convexification and volume repair
difficulty_reason: H3: Hausdorff convergence to a disk does not yield convexity or the uniform boundary regularity needed for rigidity. The new planar core first decomposes the critical nonlocal defect into one-dimensional slice energies and uses connectedness to transfer interval filling/expansion monotonicity to the convex hull. That competitor has the wrong area, so the author develops uniform normal/cone control for convex sets trapped between nearby disks, uses only the finite first moment to compare the dilation boundary term with perimeter, and proves strict energy decrease after rescaling the hull to the prescribed area. This repairs volume at the variational level without assuming unavailable uniform smoothness orG integrability. The weakerH1-H2 convexity result and its nearly-circular consequence then combine with the separately retained all-dimensional local stability input to giveTheoremA underH1-H3. The independent H3 burden here is the global planar geometric construction/strict volume repair; the local kernel Taylor core is reused from the other unit, not charged again.
